title: Calixtus: God works through the preached word unless men love darkness
source_text: VI. Eandem doctrinam tradit & distinctius explicat Georgius Calixtus, antehac Theologiae in Academia Julia Professor, Epitome Theologiae ex ore dictantis excepta. Ibi enim tractatu de ministerio verbi pagina 241. docet, quando minister verbi legalem & Evangelicam doctrinam hominibus proponit, Deum per hoc suum medium & instrumentum efficacem esse, & in cordibus humanis contritionem de commissis peccatis, fiduciam in meritum Christi, peccatorum odium, novaeque vitae studium excitare, nisi tamen ipsi homines suapte pertinacia & pervicacia tenebras magis diligant quam lucem.
pass_a_gloss: VI. The same doctrine Georg Calixtus, formerly Professor of Theology in the Julian Academy, teaches & explains more distinctly, in the Epitome of Theology taken down from his dictation. For there in the treatise on the ministry of the word page 241. he teaches, that when the minister of the word sets forth the doctrine of the Law & the Gospel to men, God is efficacious through this his means & instrument, & excites in human hearts contrition for sins committed, trust in the merit of Christ, hatred of sins, and zeal for a new life, unless however men themselves by their own obstinacy & stubbornness love darkness rather than light.
pass_b_english: Thesis VI. Georg Calixtus, formerly professor of theology at the Academia Julia, teaches the same doctrine and explains it more clearly in his Epitome of Theology, taken down as he dictated it. In the treatise on the ministry of the word, page 241, he teaches that when a minister of the word puts the teaching of the Law and of the Gospel before people, God is at work through this means and instrument of his.

Through it God rouses in human hearts sorrow for sins committed, trust in Christ's merit, hatred of sin, and eagerness for a new life, unless people, through their own stubbornness and obstinacy, love darkness more than light.
